components.css: :host{--bg:#fafafa;--sheet:#fff;--sunk:#f2f2f2;--line:#e6e6e6;--line-strong:#cfcfcf;--ink:#111;--ink-2:#3a3a3a;--muted:#6b6b6b;--accent:#a6c23f;--bar:#c9c9c9;--ease-out:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);--font:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:ui-monospace,'SF Mono',Menlo,Consolas,monospace;font-family:var(--font);}.ds-ledger{background:var(--ink);color:#f1f1f1;border-radius:16px;padding:28px 32px 12px}.ds-ledger h3{margin:0 0 18px;font-size:1.25rem;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-0.02em;color:#fff}.ds-ledger h3 span{margin-left:8px;color:#8f8f8f;font-weight:500}.ds-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(120px,168px) minmax(0,1fr) 36px;align-items:center;gap:16px;padding:12px 0;border-top:1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1)}.ds-row p{margin:0;line-height:1.5}.ds-ltype{color:#9a9a9a;font-size:0.8125rem;font-weight:500}.ds-ledger code{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:0.86em;background:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1);color:#fff;border-radius:4px;padding:0.08em 0.36em}.ds-proof{display:grid;place-items:center;width:32px;height:32px;border-radius:50%;border:1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.22);color:#fff;transition:background-color 160ms var(--ease-out),border-color 160ms var(--ease-out),transform 200ms var(--ease-out)}.ds-proof svg{width:16px;height:16px;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.6;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round}.ds-proof:hover{background:#fff;color:var(--ink);border-color:#fff;transform:translateX(2px)}.ds-proof:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #fff;outline-offset:2px}

components.css: :host{--bg:#fafafa;--sheet:#fff;--sunk:#f2f2f2;--line:#e6e6e6;--line-strong:#cfcfcf;--ink:#111;--ink-2:#3a3a3a;--muted:#6b6b6b;--accent:#a6c23f;--bar:#c9c9c9;--ease-out:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);--font:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:ui-monospace,'SF Mono',Menlo,Consolas,monospace;font-family:var(--font);}.ds-sheet{background:var(--sheet);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:16px;box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(17 17 17 / 0.04),0 12px 32px -20px rgb(17 17 17 / 0.12);padding:28px 32px;color:var(--ink);max-width:420px}.ds-sheet h3{margin:0 0 16px;font-size:1.1875rem;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-0.02em}.ds-sheet h3 small{display:block;margin-top:4px;color:var(--muted);font-size:0.875rem;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:0}.ds-kv{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;font-size:0.875rem}.ds-kv th,.ds-kv td{padding:7px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}.ds-kv tr:first-child th,.ds-kv tr:first-child td{border-top:1px solid var(--line)}.ds-kv th{text-align:left;color:var(--muted);font-weight:400}.ds-kv td{text-align:right}.ds-kv .is-alert th,.ds-kv .is-alert td{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}.ds-kv .is-alert th::before{content:'';display:inline-block;width:6px;height:6px;margin:0 8px 1px 0;border-radius:50%;background:var(--ink)}.ds-chart{margin:20px 0 0}.ds-bars{display:flex;align-items:flex-end;gap:2px;height:88px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-strong)}.ds-bars span{flex:1;background:var(--bar);transition:background-color 90ms linear}.ds-bars span:hover{background:var(--ink)}.ds-readout{min-height:1.5em;margin-top:8px;color:var(--muted);font:0.75rem/1.5 var(--mono);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-readout b{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}

narrative.overview:
The report is an analysis document set in one neutral scale. Near-white ground, white sheets on hairlines, near-black ink, and a ladder of greys carry everything; hue is almost absent. Every claim the report makes has a place where it is proven: an alert is a plain sentence in the ledger, and its round arrow lands on the variable sheet whose table and chart demonstrate it. Exact numbers are always one hover away, read out in a monospace strip under the chart rather than in floating tooltips.

Density is high but calm. A sticky left index holds sections and a filterable list of every variable with its type and alert count; the main column opens with a large title, a hairline-split stats strip, and the inverted ledger, so the state of the data is legible in the first viewport. Below, each variable is a white sheet with key/value tables, a mini chart and a "more details" disclosure.

Emphasis is carried by contrast, never by colour. The one inverted near-black panel is the alert ledger; the one chromatic token is a small olive marker that only ever signals "you are here" or "this one".
keyCharacteristics: One neutral scale; ink #111111 on near-white, greys for hierarchy.
The alert ledger is the only inverted surface.
A single olive marker for position, hover guide and arrival, never for text or data categories (correlation's negative pole is the one data exception).
Figtree at 400/500/600, tabular figures everywhere numbers sit in columns, monospace only for values and readouts.
Hairlines, soft radii, almost no shadow.

rules.name: The Contrast Not Hue Rule
rules.body: Severity is carried by inversion and weight: the ledger is ink, alert rows in key/value tables go 600 weight with an ink dot, warning badges go solid ink. No red, amber or green status colours.

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: Olive marks position and focus of attention, at dot, line or ring scale. If it covers an area or carries a word, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Grey Series Rule
rules.body: Comparison series are greys plus dashes. Olive is never a series colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can sit above another number uses tabular figures: stats, tables, counts, badges, axes, readouts.

rules.name: The Mono Is Instrumentation Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for values and readouts (code, column names, chart readouts), not for labels or headings.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separate with a 1px #e6e6e6 rule or a ground step before reaching for a shadow. A new surface that needs a shadow to be seen is in the wrong tone.

dos: Do keep every surface in the neutral scale and let the ledger be the single inverted panel.
Do pair each alert with a link to the sheet or chart that proves it, and ring the target in olive for 1.6s on arrival.
Do show exact values in the mono readout under each chart (12px, muted, bold ink value).
Do use tabular figures for every number in a column, stat, badge or axis.
Do separate with 1px #e6e6e6 hairlines and the bg-to-sheet step; keep the sheet shadow as the only resting shadow.
Do distinguish comparison datasets by grey tone and dash pattern.
Do hatch "other", missing and redacted values instead of colouring them.
donts: Don't introduce status hues (red, amber, green) for alerts or badges; severity is ink and weight.
Don't use the olive accent for text, filled areas, or comparison series.
Don't put alerts behind a tab or above-the-fold tabs in the overview.
Don't set labels or headings in monospace.
Don't add floating chart tooltips in place of the fixed readout.
